name: Organic looped-sample unison-voicing lush pad
goal: Build lush organic pads by looping acoustic samples as pseudo-oscillators (crossfaded loops), stacking complementary body+air samples, applying chordal unison voicings (fifths/sus4), light detune/spread, long amp swell, optional WT/analog stabilizers, multiband grit/width, LFO+random filter / pitch-drift / WT motion, then convolution+long reverb space.

source.title: Phase Plant | Creating Lush Organic Pads

prerequisites: Sampler or synth sampler osc with loop crossfade, unison chord modes, filters, multiband FX, reverb
constraints: Ground every step in the source YouTube-provided captions; do not invent UI or settings.
Original synthesis only — map brand UI (Serum/Vital/Pigments/Phase Plant/etc.) to portable osc/filter/FX roles for a browser or generic hybrid synth; never rip presets, wavetables, or samples.
Prefer transferable signal-flow and motion relationships over vendor-specific preset names.
Use original or licensed samples; do not rip vendor libraries named in the video.
If unison chord modes are unavailable, emulate with multiple pitched sampler voices.

steps.action: Load an acoustic sample; loop with crossfade so the loop point is inaudible — treat it as a static organic oscillator.
Layer a second contrasting organic loop (body vs air).
Apply unison chord voicings (e.g. fifths on one, sus4 on the other); add tasteful detune/spread; amp env with soft attack and slightly reduced sustain for swell-then-settle.
Add low-level WT + analog/saw stabilizers with mild unison for synthetic glue; macro to bring body in as needed.
Post FX: ensemble/flanger/filter experiments; multiband — saturate lows, light ring-mod in mids, stereo widen+chorus on highs; light glue saturation/EQ/dynamics.
Mod: LFO + random → filter (never identical motion); random → global fine pitch drift; random → WT position; aftertouch→filter; velocity→volume; macros for detune and cutoff.
Space: convolution or character reverb from original impulse (~wet) plus long lush reverb (~15s, mostly wet) for dimension.

verification: Unison/voicing yields multi-note richness from single keys
